newsitem.title: UK: Eurobonds see spread on Turkey widen around 20 b.p.
newsitem.headline: Eurobonds see spread on Turkey widen around 20 b.p.

text.p: The primary market saw another active day of issuance on Wednesday with Turkey's debut lire-denominated deal selling
slowly, which saw the spread on the 300 billion lire
five-year offering widen around 20 basis points from a
launch of 246 basis points over, traders said.
** Moscow will would launch its first Eurobond by March 15.
The 300 billion lire five-year bond was launched to yield 246 basis points over government paper via joint lead managers Chase and Banca Commerciale Italiana.
The paper pays a 9.0 percent coupon.
"Some people feel they need a bit more time to assess the credit," a syndicate official said.
In January, Moody's Investors Service said it was considering cutting Turkey's Ba3 long-term foreign currency debt rating. Turkey is rated B by Standard & Poor's.
A Turkish minister said last week Moody's was unlikely to downgrade the country's foreign debt.

Turkey successfully raised 500 million marks in January. Dealers said it was easier for Turkey to raise funds in marks than in other currencies because of the large amounts of expatriate Turkish funds in Germany.
